text: Howard Okonjo opens and closes this board meeting; Mara Voss is in the room to defend any number a director pushes on. Howard frames the headline and makes the ask — that's the CISO's job when speaking to a body that evaluates risk, not engineering detail.

The results: standing OT/SCADA admin access cut from 17 untracked accounts to 13 governed ones, dual-cloud identity consolidated for the pilot segment, and shadow local accounts removed entirely. Real numbers, from a real quarter.

The discrepancy gets disclosed plainly, not softened: two independent methods checked the same access and disagreed, the root cause was found and fixed, and both now agree. That sentence is evidence the program is working, not a confession to bury.

The ask closes the report: fund and staff extending zero-trust segmentation and the corrected audit methodology to the next OT segment. Without an ask, a board report is just a status update. Next lesson: the question that tests all of this.
